audit.whatIsWrong: The full-layer chart reads Talon / Skill / Skill / Skill / Diana / Skill / Skill while the content layer and packet.levelChart both read Diana / Talon / Talon / Talon / Diana / Diana / Diana. Five of seven rows disagree across layers.
audit.why: Talon's window is levels 2-5: Rake at 9s rank 1 plus Noxian Diplomacy's 575-range leap and crit, cashed through three Blade's End stacks, beats a single Pale Cascade. Diana takes level 1 (900 Q vs 650 W) and everything from 6 onward.
audit.corrected: Move the full-layer sides onto the content values and rewrite the whys on rows 1, 2 and 3 so they describe Talon winning those stages.

audit.why: Level 2-5 Talon combo spike, level 6 Moonfall (100s) against Shadow Assault (100s at rank 1), first item extended-trade flip, late reset chains. The content spikes already frame it correctly once the fabricated ability name is removed.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page states that Moonlight (Q) and Moonfall (R) both reveal — Diana is one of the few mid champions who answers Shadow Assault's invisibility directly. breakdown.cooldowns also contains no digit.
audit.why: ownerKit flags revealsStealth on both Q and R; Riot's text for Shadow Assault is explicit that Talon becomes Invisible and the blades converge when he emerges. A revealed Talon inside 475 is a melee target inside Moonfall.
audit.corrected: State the reveal in breakdown.cooldowns and breakdown.carry, with Rake 9s, Noxian Diplomacy 8s and Shadow Assault 100s.

audit.whatIsWrong: "Cutthroat" is a fabricated ability name appearing in content spikes[0].text and wants.foe[1]; Talon's Q is Noxian Diplomacy. Separately, content early, spikes[0].text and wants.foe[0] all credit Shadow Assault with the wall-vault, which is Assassin's Path (E).
audit.why: Riot's text: Assassin's Path vaults over any terrain at zero cost, putting that piece of terrain on a long cooldown; Shadow Assault is the invisibility ultimate. Conflating them tells the reader to ward for the wrong ability at the wrong level.
audit.corrected: Every affected string is rewritten below with the real names.

edits.before: W shield-trade window: orbs absorb his poke and pay it back on the three-hit passive.
edits.after: Rake is 9s at rank 1 and hits twice — his level 2 combo out-damages one Pale Cascade.

edits.before: E pull joins... no — your dash threat begins: Q-mark into E reset chases are live; trade on every landed crescent.
edits.after: Noxian Diplomacy leaps from 575 and crits in melee; with Rake behind it his level 3 all-in beats your Q-E trade.

edits.before: Mark-dash trades on cooldown — Q, E to the mark, passive three-hit, walk. The lane respects the curve now.
edits.after: Assassin's Path costs nothing and vaults any wall — he picks the fight, and Blade's End bleeds you after it.

edits.before: - Talon Rake: matchup-defining — The boomerang return is most of his lane damage — stand off the return line. Check it before every step-up. - W Pale Cascade is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Rake is 9s at rank 1 and the returning blades carry most of it — stand off the return line and step up on that 9s. - Noxian Diplomacy is 8s at rank 1. - Pale Cascade is 15s. - Shadow Assault is 100s, and your Q and R both reveal him out of it.

edits.before: Q through the wave onto his chest, E the mark, three-hit string, walk — the phase trade he answers after you've left.
edits.after: Assassin's Path is free but the wall it uses goes on a long cooldown — Q-mark him after he vaults and the exit is gone.

edits.before: Dashing onto an unmarked target with W down — Diana without the reset or the shield is a melee mage donating proximity.
edits.after: Chasing him into his own wall line hands him a free Assassin's Path vault while your Lunar Rush sits on 22 seconds.

edits.before: Talon wins by landing Rake, denying your pattern, and front-loading the violence while your kit is still stretching.
edits.after: Talon wins by opening with Rake, leaping in on Noxian Diplomacy, and cashing three Blade's End stacks before your W lands.

edits.before: Carry through the dive — mark, dash, pull, delete; your R turns their teamfight spacing into a suggestion.
edits.after: Carry by holding Q and R for his Shadow Assault — both reveal him, and a revealed Talon is just a melee target.

edits.before: Talon's Rake-Cutthroat-Rake combo hits like a truck from levels 2-5 and his Shadow Assault lets him dive in from a wall or brush undetected, punishing you hard if you're pushed up without vision.
edits.after: Talon's Rake into Noxian Diplomacy hits like a truck from levels 2-5, and Assassin's Path vaults him in over any wall, punishing you hard if you are pushed up without vision on the sides.

edits.before: Use Shadow Assault to engage from stealth near terrain
edits.after: Vault a side wall with Assassin's Path to open on you

edits.before: Land the full Rake-AA-Cutthroat combo before you can react
edits.after: Land the full Rake-AA-Noxian Diplomacy combo before you react

edits.before: Talon is genuinely dangerous from levels 2 through 5, since his combo damage output is some of the highest in the game at those levels and Shadow Assault lets him engage from stealth near any wall or brush, punishing overextension severely. Play cautiously, ward the walls near your lane, and avoid pushing the wave too far without vision, since a clean combo from him can delete a big chunk of your HP or outright kill you. This is one of the few windows where you should play reactively rather than trying to force trades.

notes: Chart: full layer read Talon/Skill/Skill/Skill/Diana/Skill/Skill; content win[] and packet.levelChart agree on Diana/Talon/Talon/Talon/Diana/Diana/Diana. I moved the full layer onto the content values, so there is NO paired win[N] edit — win[N] is already correct on every row and an edit whose before equals its after cannot be written. Rows 1, 2 and 3 had whys describing Diana winning under a row that now says Talon; all three were rewritten in this same proposal so no row argues with itself. 'Cutthroat' is a fabricated name (it was Talon's old E) and appeared twice in the content layer — both killed. Shadow Assault was credited with the wall-vault in three places; that is Assassin's Path. packet.suspectNames flagged wants.foe[0] 'Use Shadow Assault' as a near-miss name — the NAME was fine, the ATTRIBUTION was not, which the distance check cannot see. Diana's Q and R both carry revealsStealth and that is the single most valuable unstated interaction in this matchup; it is now in breakdown.cooldowns and breakdown.carry.
